markdownEditor.sample:
# Project Name

Write a one-line intro. The preview on the right updates as you type, and your draft is **autosaved in this browser**.

> [!TIP]
> When you're done, click **Copy rich text** below to paste into a blog or Notion, or save as .md / .html.

## Text formatting

**Bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd>
Write links like [ToolHub](https://toolhub.ai.kr), or just paste a URL: https://toolhub.ai.kr

## Lists

- Bullet list
  - Indent two spaces for a sub-item
- Press Enter and the next bullet is added for you

1. Install
2. Configure
3. Run

- [x] Write the draft
- [ ] Paste an image (Ctrl+V)

## Code

```javascript
// syntax highlighting
function greet(name) {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`
}
```

## Table

| Feature | Shortcut | Note |
|:--------|:--------:|-----:|
| Bold | Ctrl+B | Wraps the selection |
| Link | Ctrl+K | `[text](URL)` |
| Save | Ctrl+S | Downloads .md |

## Footnotes

Markdown was created by John Gruber in 2004[^1].

[^1]: The extended syntax used on GitHub is called GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown).

whatIs.title: What is this tool?
whatIs.description: A Markdown editor for drafting GitHub READMEs, tech blog posts and Notion pages with an instant preview. It supports GitHub (GFM) syntax such as tables, task lists, footnotes and alert boxes, plus code syntax highlighting, and autosaves your draft in this browser. Copy the result with formatting into a blog or Notion, or download it as .md or .html. Everything runs in your browser; nothing is sent to a server.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: Type Markdown in the editor and the preview updates instantly. On mobile, switch with the Edit/Preview tabs at the top.
Use the toolbar or shortcuts (Ctrl+B bold, Ctrl+I italic, Ctrl+K link) to wrap the selected text.
Paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V or drop an image file to embed it in the document.
Open the table of contents to jump to a heading in the preview.
When finished, choose Copy rich text (blog/Notion), copy Markdown/HTML, or download .md/.html.

tips.title: Tips
items: Add a language after the fence (```python) to color keywords, strings and comments.
Press Enter on a list line to add the next marker (-, 2., - [ ]) automatically; press Enter on an empty item to end the list.
README badges are written as [![name](badge image URL)](link URL).
Use Copy rich text for Notion; for blogs use Copy rich text or paste Copy HTML into the HTML mode.
Pasted images are embedded as base64 and make the file large. For blog posts, upload images in the blog editor instead.

items.a: A lightweight markup language that formats text with simple symbols like #, * and -. It is widely used on GitHub, Notion, Slack and many blogs.

Yes. When you pause typing, the draft is saved to this browser (localStorage) and restored next time. It is not shared with other devices or browsers and is removed if you clear site data, so download important documents as .md.
Paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V or drop an image file to embed it directly (base64, up to 2MB). For hosted images, use ![description](image URL).

items.q: Is my text sent to a server?
items.a: No. Rendering, saving and exporting all happen in your browser. The preview is rendered safely, blocking scripts and dangerous links such as javascript:.

items.q: Line breaks look different from GitHub.
items.a: This preview turns every single line break into a new line, like a blog or notes app. In a GitHub README, separate paragraphs with a blank line or end a line with two spaces to force a break.
